comments.author: petaciokas
comments.body:
Today I found out a new fast but expensive way to grind casting :)

If you are portuguese, you can invest in Lisbon, buy copper ore there, make copper, buy copper plating at carpenter in shipyard and make light (or weathered) copper platings using "Making extra metal armouring" book (which you can buy at craftsman). Well, it is a little bit expensive, but it gives nice skill proficiency. I am at rank 15 and i get 5 skill points from each production. So at rank 9 I think you will get even more.
Actually now I am making light iron platings using Rank 10 recipe from the same book. From 600 iron I plan to get about 5000 skill points. And it will cost me about 30-40 mil :) But I don't care much about it, because i really want to max casting :)

comments.author: petaciokas
comments.body:
If you don't want to spend a lot of money, at your rank I advice you to buy Iron ore in Algiers (bring some equipment with disguise), sail to Barcelona while making Iron.
Buy Steel in Barcelona and sail back to Algiers while making Shamshirs (Rank 8 recipe from "Weapon manufacturing techniques" book).
This recipe only needs 1 iron +1 steel and gives nice skill proficiency.

You will get more proficiency improving copper plates, but this way is more expensive. On the other hand, improving copper plates is not so expensive as improving iron plates :)
If you have high mineral trading and wares trading then you can try shamshirs. Also making shamshirs involves sailing and producing at sea without clicking mouse too much.
Improving plates involves many mouse clickings and no sailing.

comments.author: Guilder
comments.body:
An unlisted alternative +1 Casting weapon also exists: Knight's Stiletto

Pros: KS has 65 durability as opposed to the Shipwright's hammer which only has 5. The hammer is needed for certain recipes, but the KS is not.
Cons: The KS requires both an Adept of Ages title, and 500 Casting contribution to Florence per production (see its page for full details).

The KS seems a better long-term option for dedicated casters than the hammer, to me. Judge for yourself whether or not it's worth acquiring one.
